DESCRIPTION: The definition of Y_union(t) in §8.2 (Composite System Emergence) is ambiguous when the same finding is reported by multiple models with different abstraction indices. The formula Y_union(t) = |⋃ F_i(t)| · H̄_union(t) requires a unique abstraction index for each finding in the union. If two models report the same finding with different H(x) values, the framework must specify how to resolve the conflict (e.g., take the maximum, the average, or the value from the first model). Without this rule, the emergence condition Y_composite(t) > Y_union(t) + k·σ̂(Y) is not well‑defined.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a deterministic rule for merging duplicate findings in the union set, e.g., “When the same finding appears in multiple individual sets, use the maximum H(x) value among the duplicates for the union set.”
